headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Open Interpreter’s broad filesystem/network access can ingest and act on agentic-flow outputs by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads/writes the filesystem and clipboard by default. That creates a plausible bridge where agent_a output is copied into agent_b or shared files are parsed as instructions. The pathway is not proven, but it exists in default-ish desktop workflows and is more than manual copy-paste alone.
conditions: IF agent_a output is transferred into a shared file or clipboard that agent_b parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF agent_b is run with auto-run or equivalent permissive execution, malicious instructions in agent_a output can be executed.
mitigations: Disable auto-run / require confirmation for every code block.
Keep agent_a and agent_b on separate workspaces or user accounts.
Strip instructions from agent_a outputs before handing them to agent_b.
Use a provenance tag or wrapper format for all inter-agent messages.
requires-engineering: add a parser that rejects imperative text in untrusted inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has broad filesystem access to the entire user machine and broad network egress, while agent_a touches repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets (Ed25519 signatures). If agent_a writes artifacts into shared files or stdout that agent_b can read, agent_b can exfiltrate them through its network path. This is a default-dangerous desktop pairing.
conditions: IF agent_a stores prompts, signatures, or repository metadata in a shared directory, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b is allowed to send retrieved file contents to configured model providers, those contents can leave the machine.
mitigations: Place agent_a and agent_b in separate directories with OS permissions.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running agent_b.
Restrict agent_b network egress to a local-only or allowlisted sink.
Run agent_b in a throwaway user profile for sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, and modify git state. agent_b also writes the filesystem and shares state via filesystem across instances, while agent_a can run multiple instances and use MCP. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt state or overwrite each other without locking, which is a high-risk default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent commits or file edits can race.
IF either agent runs without external locking, filesystem state can be overwritten or corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout or working directory.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Disable one agent’s write access during the other’s run.
Use branch-per-agent workflows with manual merge review.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs from MCP-driven workflows, and agent_b can act on local files and shell commands. If agent_b treats agent_a’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. The pair does not prove blind trust, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF agent_a emits malformed or hallucinated instructions, agent_b may execute them.
mitigations: Require a human review step before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Have agent_b verify claims against source files before editing.
Limit agent_b to read-only mode until outputs are checked.
Log agent_a outputs separately from executable commands.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures; agent_b can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated or sensitive data is present on that machine, agent_b’s broad local access can violate residency or retention expectations even though no specific certification mismatch is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the local machine, agent_b can access it beyond intended scope.
IF agent_a writes prompts or metadata into retained files, those files may persist under agent_b’s broader access model.
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the shared machine.
Use separate retention policies for each agent’s outputs.
Delete temporary files immediately after each run.
Restrict agent_b to a dedicated data directory.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data classification and retention controls.
